therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: treatment-naive adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Mean change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 12

results.target_engagement_evidence: Dose-dependent reductions in HbA1c, FPG, and fructosamine consistent with SGLT2 inhibition
biomarker_changes: HbA1c reduced by up to -0.85% (1000 mg QD) vs -0.19% placebo at Week 12
FPG reduced by up to -1.63 mmol/L (250 mg BID) vs -0.50 mmol/L placebo
Fructosamine reduced by up to -37.9 µmol/L (1000 mg QD) vs -1.4 µmol/L placebo
Body weight reduced by up to -2.54 kg (250 mg QD) vs -1.03 kg placebo
HDL-c increased modestly across GSK189075 arms
subgroup_findings: HbA1c responders (<7%): 250 mg BID had highest count (15 vs 7 placebo)
FPG responders (reduction ≥1.7 mmol/L): 250 mg BID had highest count (19 vs 5 placebo, OR=13.01, p<0.001)
Pioglitazone 30 mg QD showed HbA1c change of -0.38% (not significantly different from placebo, p=0.337)
safety_signals: Low rates of hypoglycemia across all arms (0-2 participants per arm)
Orthostatic HR standing high observed in 5-7 participants per active arm vs 4 placebo
Abnormal ECG findings in 7-14 participants per arm; no clear dose-dependent pattern
2 SAEs reported: 1 cholelithiasis (GSK189075 100 mg QD), 1 scapula fracture (GSK189075 250 mg BID)
Low bicarbonate/CO2 observed in some GSK189075 arms (consistent with SGLT2 inhibitor class effect)
Low calcium observed in some GSK189075 arms

dose_info.dose: 100 mg, 250 mg, 500 mg, 1000 mg QD; 250 mg BID
dose_info.schedule: once daily (QD) or twice daily (BID) for 12 weeks

context.comparator: placebo (and pioglitazone 30 mg QD active comparator)
